ui.now_intro: This is a now page: what I am up to at the moment, as opposed to what I once said I would do.

illustrator.tagline: Pictures for books, posters and the odd birthday card.
illustrator.desc: {brand}: illustrator and printmaker in {city}. Picture books, posters and linocuts.
illustrator.bio: I draw pictures for picture books and posters, and cut linocuts for anyone who asks politely.
about: I draw for a living, mostly for picture books and the occasional poster. I work from a small room in {city} with a window onto a parking lot, which I draw as if it were a lake.
Before illustration I studied textile printing, and the habit of thinking in layers never quite left. Most of my pictures are built from three or four flat colors.
facts: Working with pen, ink and linocut

projects.d: A picture book about a year in one small field, made with a local press.
Twelve linocuts of stalls, shoppers and one very smug pigeon.
Six cards, printed by hand in editions of two hundred.

now: Finishing the last spreads of a picture book about weather
Learning to cut a four-color linocut without losing my temper

translator.tagline: Careful translations of fiction, essays and the occasional manual.
translator.desc: {brand}: translator from German into English, working on fiction and essays from {city}.
translator.bio: I translate German into English, mostly fiction and essays, and read everything aloud twice.
about: I translate from German into English, mostly fiction and essays, and sometimes the instruction manual of a thing that deserves better writing.
I work slowly, read everything aloud twice and send a note about every sentence I could not decide on. Editors tell me this is either charming or maddening.

projects.t: A novel about a lighthouse keeper
projects.d: Four hundred pages of weather and regret, translated over fourteen months.
A collection of short pieces by a writer who went everywhere on foot.
Texts for an exhibition of textiles, with more adjectives than I would have chosen.

now: Revising the translation of a long novel
Reading essays I might suggest to a publisher
Updating my glossary of nautical terms

potter.tagline: Plain bowls, mugs and plates, made in small batches.
potter.desc: {brand}: potter in {city}. Everyday stoneware, thrown on the wheel.
potter.bio: I throw plain stoneware on the wheel and fire it in small batches.
about: I make functional pottery in a studio shared with three other makers in {city}. Everything is thrown on the wheel and fired to stoneware.
I like pots that disappear into daily use: a mug that fits the hand, a bowl that does not tip. The glazes are mostly iron and ash, and they change a little in every firing.

projects.d: Plates, bowls and mugs in an oatmeal glaze that did not come out the same twice.
Thirty small bowls, each a little different, made for a tea house.
A wall of hand-pressed tiles for a kitchen, in four greens.

now: Testing an ash glaze made from a neighbor's bonfire
Making room on the kiln shelves for winter orders

developer.tagline: Small, quiet programs that do one thing and stay out of the way.
developer.desc: {brand}: developer of small tools in {city}. A notes app, a calendar and a few command line programs.
developer.bio: I write small tools for people who work with words and numbers, and try to ship them finished.
about: I write small tools for people who work with words and numbers: a notes app, a few command line programs, a calendar that only shows what matters today.
I build things slowly and try to ship them finished. Most of what I make has fewer features than it could, which is on purpose.
facts: Writing in a few boring languages

projects.t: A notes app for the desktop
projects.d: Plain text files, fast search and no account.
Shows today and nothing else, which turns out to be enough.
One button and a weekly summary, for people who dislike timesheets.

now: Tidying the code of the notes app
Thinking about a smaller version of everything
